## The metric library

What a metric must say, who may add, change, remove, link and unlink one, and which metric measures a goal, for which slice.

### The rule

A **metric** is one number defined once per workspace, so every goal about it means the same thing. It has a **name**, a **unit** and a **direction** (higher or lower is better): those three are required. Everything else is optional: what it **means and how it’s calculated**, **decimals** (0 to 4; 0 when not said), its **source** and who owns that source (text), how often the source **refreshes** (live, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or not said), its **owner** (a person in the workspace: whoever added it, unless they hand it on) and **caveats**. A name is 3 to 120 characters and no other metric in use shares it, whatever the case; a unit is up to 20 characters; each text up to 2,000. Text is trimmed before it’s checked.

**Who may.** Anyone adds a metric. Only its owner or an admin changes or removes it. Only a goal’s owner or an admin says which metric measures the goal, or stops it being measured by one, whoever owns the metric.

**Measuring a goal.** A goal is measured by at most one metric, for one **slice**: a team’s number, or the whole company’s. The goal’s own target is the target in that metric (a number to move: its plan’s target; a number to keep in range: its limit); nothing is copied. A goal with dated stages has no number, so no metric measures it. The goal and the metric must have the same unit, any case. A goal aiming the other way from the metric’s better direction (planned to go up when lower is better, or kept at least a level when lower is better) is linked with a warning, since a guardrail may mean it. So is a goal that keeps more decimal places than its metric. The goal's target in the metric is shown as every number is ([numbers and names](../../core/rules/numbers-and-names.md)): at the goal's decimals, digits grouped, with its unit. Linking again with the same metric and slice changes nothing; another metric or slice is a change.

**Logged, never lost.** Every change is in the change log as a metric change (adding, changing field by field, removing, restoring; linking and unlinking on the goal it measures). Only a metric no goal has ever been measured by can be removed (deleted); one that has is retired instead (MT3, rule 10). Removing keeps its row; Undo straight after puts it back, and so does restoring it later from Recently removed. Unlinking keeps the link’s row too, and Undo puts it back.

### Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** Two people changing the same metric at once: the later save wins (metrics carry no version yet, unlike goals and reviews).
- **Not self-explanatory:** The words for a slice are the team’s name, or “The whole company”; the change log says “for the whole company” or “for <team>”.

## The library as a place

Which metrics the library lists for a search and its filters, in what order (rule 1); a metric’s goals side by side (rule 2); and what a metric still needs (rule 3).

### The rule

Each rule takes plain rows: every metric, every goal’s link, the ids of the running cycle’s **live goals** (not removed, not stopped), the people, and the moment it is judged at. A **link in force** is one not unlinked, to a live goal. Removed metrics are never listed.

**Rule 1. Finding metrics** (`findMetrics`). A search matches when every word typed starts a word of the metric’s name, unit, “lower is better” or “higher is better”, its owner’s name, its meaning or its source, ignoring case and accents ([finding things](../../core/rules/finding.md), rule 1). Filters, each optional: a **unit** (the same, any case); a **team** (a link in force whose slice is that team) or `company` (a link in force for the whole company); an **owner**; a **direction**; **unused** (no link in force); **sort out** (rule 3 says it needs something, whoever is looking). Order: **A to Z** by name, ignoring case and accents (the default); **most goals first** (links in force), then A to Z; **changed lately** (`updatedAt`, latest first), then A to Z. Fifty a page; a page past the last shows the last.

**Rule 2. A metric’s goals** (`metricGoals`). One row per link in force to a live goal: its status, its slice in words (the team’s name, “The whole company”, or “A removed team”), its latest number as the goal shows it (“No value yet”), its target with its week (“24 hours by year end”), where it stands against plan as the scorecard says it (“9 hours behind plan”; a goal kept in range says its room to the limit, “Near the 2.0% limit”) and its owner: each from the goal’s own summary, never worked out again. Worst status first (on track, then at risk and no recent update, then off track, by the status rank), then by slice name, then title. Under them, `summaryLine`: when two or more rows have a number and every one of them is in the same unit with the same decimals, “Lowest now: {slice}, {now}. Highest: {slice}, {now}.” (the lowest number, then the highest; ties by slice name); otherwise nothing.

**Rule 3. What a metric needs** (`metricNeeds`), in this order: **no-owner** (“It has no owner” when its owner is no one in the workspace; “Its owner has left” when they have left), **no-meaning** (“No meaning yet”), **no-source** (“No source named”), **unused** (“No goal uses it”: no link in force, and it was added more than 14 days before the moment). Each has one button: “Choose an owner”, “Say what it means”, “Say where the number comes from” (each opens the metric’s form at that field), or “See goals in {unit}” (Goals, every goal, searched for its unit). A library row says the first, with “and {k} more” after it; only the metric’s owner and admins see them.

**Addresses.** A metric’s page is `/metrics/<slug>`, its slug being its id without `metric_`. Wednesday’s addresses under Data lead on (`movedMetrics`): `/data/metrics` to `/metrics`, `?m=<id>` to the metric, `?m=<id>&edit` to its form, `?new` to a new one, keeping the rest of the query. Its rows are scored in [the conformance data](../../conformance/README.md) (`metrics.csv`).

### Requirements

- `METRICS-LIBRARY`: Anyone can find a metric, read what it means, and see every goal measured by it side by side (ML1). Metrics (/metrics, in the menu after People; on a phone under More) lists every metric in use A to Z ignoring case and accents, 50 a page; a search matches the name, unit, "lower is better" or "higher is better", the owner and the meaning; filters for the unit, the team or the whole company a goal measures it for, the owner, which way is better, no goals, and something to sort out; sorts A to Z, most goals first and changed lately; everything in the address. A row links to the metric, says its unit, direction and owner, and its goals by status as shape and word, worst first. A metric's page says what it means and how it's calculated, then its goals as a table (status, goal, for, now, target with its week, against plan, owner), worst first, with the lowest and highest now when two or more have a number, then its source, the source's owner, refresh, caveats and who added and last changed it. Its owner and admins see what it still needs and can change or remove it; everyone else sees who can. A goal's summary says what measures it; a person's page lists the metrics they own and a team's the metrics its goals use. Old addresses under /data/metrics lead to the library, a metric or the form.

## “Measured by”, found by typing

What choosing a metric in a goal form fills in (rule 5), what stops the goal being saved with it, and the words the metric finder gives each metric.

### The rule

A goal's metric is chosen where the goal is made or changed, by typing part of its name, unit, direction, owner, meaning or source (rule 1's words). Each metric reads as two lines: its name, then “{unit} · {lower|higher} is better · {owner}” (“no owner” when it has none, or they have left). Before anything is typed, up to six are offered: those chosen lately, then those the viewer's team's goals are measured by, then the most used. A metric removed since it was chosen still reads by its name.

**Rule 5. What a chosen metric sets on the form** (`measureDefaults`). On a **new** goal whose unit and decimal places are still the form's own (nobody typed them), choosing a metric sets both from it, and the form says so in one line instead of the two fields: “{unit}, {decimals in words}, {lower|higher} is better: from the metric.” “Use different ones” shows the fields again, filled from the metric. Choosing “No metric” afterwards gives them back what they held. A field the person typed is kept. On a goal that already exists nothing is set.

**What stops it** (`measureFormProblems`). A unit that differs from the metric's, any case, stops the goal being saved with that metric: “This metric is in {unit}; this goal is in {unit}.” More decimal places than the metric keeps is a warning, as linking says. A goal with dated stages has no number, so it has no “Measured by”. Which way the target lies from the start is judged when the link is saved (the metric library, above).

**For.** The goal's team (chosen at first), or the whole company; with no team chosen yet, only the whole company. Check says “Measured by {metric}, for {team | the whole company}.”

**Goals, filtered by a metric.** Goals' address takes `?metric=<id>`: the goals a metric measures now (a link in force). The filter line says “Measured by {metric}”. It is declared as data (a column of each goal's summary, the metric its link names), so a server compares the column itself.

### Limits the records hold

Faro’s database holds these as well as the rule; a rebuild holds them wherever it stores the records. The constraint names are in `spec/core/schema.sql`, which is for reading, not copying.

- The part of a metric a goal is measured by (“Which part”) has at most 60 characters; empty means all of it. (`okr_goal_metrics_part_len`)

### Requirements

- `METRICS-MEASURED-BY`: A goal's metric is chosen by typing to find it where the goal is made or changed, or added there, and fills in what the metric already says (ML2). In New goal, "Measured by" is the first field on the measure step (under the name when changing a goal), never for a goal with dated stages or for someone who may not link the goal: find-and-pick with "No metric" first, metrics in the goal's unit offered first, and "Add “…” as a new metric" last. Choosing one shows its meaning, the goal's team or the whole company under "For", and, on a new goal whose unit and decimals nobody typed, sets them from the metric and says so in one line with "Use different ones". A unit that differs stops the save with the reason. Added in place, a metric needs a name, a unit and which way is better, is owned by whoever adds it, and is chosen. Check says "Measured by {metric}, for {team}". Goals filters by the metric (?metric=, "Measured by" in the filter line), and a metric's page opens Goals filtered to it.

## Looking after metrics

A name close to one already in the library (rule 4), and what an admin is told on Workspace → About.

### The rule

**Rule 4. A close name** (`closeNames`). While a metric is added, a name of four characters or more is compared with every metric in use as sets of words: lower case, without accents and punctuation, leaving out anything in brackets and the words “the”, “of”, “per”, “for”, “in”, “a”, “rate” and “time”. Two names are close when one set contains the other, or when they share at least two words and differ by at most one. Up to two are named, closest first (fewest words apart, then A to Z). An exact match, any case, is not close: it is refused as a name already taken. The question is said, never an error, and never stops the save: “This looks like “{other}” ({unit}, {direction}, owned by {name}). Use that one, or carry on if yours is different.”

**Changing what goals rely on.** When goals in force are measured by a metric and its unit or direction is changed, the form asks first: how many goals, and how many of them will then show a warning that they differ (linking's checks). Their numbers and plans don't change.

**Workspace → About** tells admins how many metrics in use have no owner, or an owner who has left: “{n} metrics have no owner”, because an owner keeps a metric's meaning true, with See them (the library's Something to sort out).

### Limits the records hold

Faro’s database holds these as well as the rule; a rebuild holds them wherever it stores the records. The constraint names are in `spec/core/schema.sql`, which is for reading, not copying.

- Why a metric was retired has at most 300 characters. (`okr_metrics_retired_why_len`)

## Defining a metric well

What a metric still needs to say, in words and never as a score (rule 6), and the three questions adding or changing one may ask before it is saved: a close name, a unit spelt another way, a percentage that doesn’t say out of what.

### The rule

A metric is **usable** with three things: a name, a unit and which way is better. The rest can be said later, and what is still missing is said in words.

**Rule 6. What a metric still needs** (`stillToSay`). In this order: “what it means” (no meaning), “where the number comes from” (no source), “who owns that source” (not said) and “how often it refreshes” (not said). The line is “Fully defined” when nothing is missing and its owner is someone here who hasn't left; “Its owner has left.” alone when only that; otherwise “Still to say: {what is missing, with commas}.”, followed by “ Its owner has left.” when so. It is words, never a number, a percentage or a bar, and nothing sorts by it. It shows under a metric's title (for its owner and admins each item opens the form at its field), at the foot of the form, in `get_metric` (`stillToSay`) and after `save_metric` saves.

**The questions (Checks).** A Check is a question answered once, never a refusal: the metric can be saved once it is answered. Adding a metric asks all three; changing one asks only about a field that changed.
- **A close name** (`nameChecks`), up to two, closest first. *Former*: the name is one a metric in use used to have (a rename in the change log): ““{typed}” is now called “{other}”.”, answered “Use {other}” or “Add “{typed}” as a new metric”. *Letters*: lower case, without accents and punctuation, the names differ by one edit when the longer is up to 12 characters and two when longer, and aren't equal; names of 4 characters or fewer never are (“MTTR” and “MTTD”): “This is one letter from “{other}” ({unit}, {direction}, owned by {owner}, {n} goals).” *Words*: the library's rule 4: “This looks like “{other}” (…).” Both answered “Use that one” (which opens it; the draft is kept) or “Mine is different: keep it”. The same name in any case is a Must fix, not this.
- **A unit spelt another way** (`unitChecks`): lower case and without a trailing “s” or “.”, it equals a unit in use, or it is a known spelling of one in use (percent, pct, per cent → %; mins, minutes, minute → min; hrs, hr, hour → hours; secs, seconds, sec → s; dollars, $ → USD), and isn't already identical: “Other metrics here use “{u}”. Use “{u}”, or keep “{typed}”?”
- **A share that doesn't say out of what** (`meaningChecks`): the unit is %, or the name has “rate”, “share” or “ratio” and the unit is neither a time nor a count per time; the meaning is said; and it has none of “out of”, “share of”, “of all”, “of every”, “divided by”, “per ”, “÷”, “/”, “percentage of”, “proportion of”, “fraction of”. Answered “It’s right as written”. An empty meaning is never this: it is still to say.

**On the form** a Must fix shows under its field, outlined on every side and washed, with the warning mark and “Must fix”; a Check under its field, in a quiet outlined block with the warning mark, “Check” and its answers as plain buttons. Neither uses a status shape. Both show once the field is left, or on the first try to save. The foot says “{a} to fix, {b} to check.” (`countLine`; a part at zero is left out) and the completeness line. Saving is refused while a Must fix stands; with a Check unanswered, the first try scrolls to it and says “Answer the question above first.” under the button. An answered Check closes to one line with Change (“You said: mine is different.”); changing the field asks again.

**Through the AI tools**, `save_metric` returns `checks` (each with its question and answers) and saves nothing while one is unanswered; it takes `answers`: `name` “keep” or “use:<id>” (nothing is saved; the result names the metric to use), `unit` “keep” or “use”, `meaning` “as-written”.

### Limits the records hold

Faro’s database holds these as well as the rule; a rebuild holds them wherever it stores the records. The constraint names are in `spec/core/schema.sql`, which is for reading, not copying.

- A metric’s name has 1 to 120 characters. (`okr_metrics_name_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/modules/metrics/rules.ts`)
- A metric’s unit has 1 to 20 characters. (`okr_metrics_unit_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/modules/metrics/rules.ts`)
- A metric keeps 0 to 4 decimal places (a goal keeps at most 3). (`okr_metrics_decimals_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/modules/metrics/rules.ts`)
- A metric’s meaning, source, source owner and caveats each have at most 2,000 characters. (`okr_metrics_meaning_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/modules/metrics/rules.ts`)
- A metric is measured, partly measured or a gap (not measured yet); measured unless someone says otherwise. (`okr_metrics_measurement_ok`)
- What is missing from a metric’s measurement has at most 300 characters. (`okr_metrics_measurement_note_len`)

## For, which part, and what a goal takes from its metric

Which part of a team’s or the company’s number a goal is measured by (rule 7), the parts other goals on the metric use, what linking asks, and why a goal with check-ins says why it is measured differently.

### The rule

A goal measured by a metric takes two things from it: its **unit** and **which way is better** (“From the metric”: “{unit}, {decimals in words}, {lower|higher} is better.”, then “ From {source}, refreshed {refresh}.” when the metric says them). Its start, target, plan and due week stay the goal's own. A link says whose number: **For** a team or the whole company, and optionally **Which part** of it (“tier-1 services”, a region, “release builds”; at most 60 characters; empty for all of it).

**Rule 7. Parts** (`partKey`, `partsOf`, `closePart`). Two parts are one when they match lower case, without accents and punctuation, with spaces collapsed and a trailing “s” dropped from each word of four letters or more (“US” is not “U”). `partsOf` lists the distinct parts a metric's live links use, most used first, each in its most used spelling; the form offers up to five under the field (“Parts other goals on this metric use: …”, each filling the field). `closePart` finds a part in use that a typed one probably means: the same part spelt differently, or one edit away (never for parts of two characters or fewer, nor when their numbers differ: “Region 2” is not “Region 1”).

**What linking asks** (`linkChecks`, in `linkGoalMetric` and `link_goal_metric`). Must fix, which refuses the link: what the library already refuses (dated stages; a different unit), a part over 60 characters, and, on a goal with check-ins whose metric, team or part differs from its last link (removed or not, so unlinking first changes nothing), an empty **Why** (“Say why this goal is measured differently now.”, under a Why marked Required whose hint says it shows in its History; at most 300 characters). Checks, each answered once, hold the save at the form as at the tool, and focus goes to the first: another live goal of the same cycle (at every door) on the same metric, team and part (“Another goal already measures this for {slice}: “{goal}” ({key}, {owner}). Two goals on one number is unusual.” → Carry on), and, when there is none, a part spelt like one in use (“{metric} already has a part called “{other}”.” → Use “{other}” / Keep “{typed}”). Aim and decimals stay warnings, as before. The History entry says “Measured by “{metric}” for {slice} · {part}: {why}”, with a row for each of Measured by, Slice and Which part that changed.

**Shown** on a goal's About as “Measured by {metric}”, a list: For ({slice}{ · part}), What it means, From the metric, Where the number comes from (“{source} ({source owner}), refreshed {refresh}”, parts left out when empty), Caveats, This goal's own (its target), and For this goal (its own definition, only when it differs from the metric's meaning). On a metric's page each goal's For reads “{slice} · {part}”. Through the AI tools, `link_goal_metric` takes `part` and `reason`, returns `checks` and saves nothing until it gets `answers` (`part`: “keep” or “use:{part}”; `others`: “carry-on”).

## Changing, retiring and merging a metric

What kind of change a save is (rule 8), the marks a change of meaning or direction leaves on its goals (rule 9), and retiring, bringing back and merging (rule 10): a metric that changes tells its goals.

### The rule

**Rule 8. What kind of change** (`changeKinds(before, after, linkedGoals, { relabel })`). Every kind that applies, in this order: `scale` (the unit differs, goals are linked, and it isn't said to be a new label: refused), `relabel` (the same, said to be a new label: every linked goal's unit changes in the same save), `direction` (needs a reason), `meaning` (the meaning or the source differs: asks whether it is still the same number, `comparable`; when it isn't, a reason), `decimals` (fewer places than a linked goal shows: named, nothing asked). Anything else, or any change to a metric no live goal uses, is `words` and saves at once; nothing different is `none`. A reason is at most 300 characters. The goals counted (`linkedGoals`) are every one with a link in force that isn't removed, a stopped one included (it can be restored). The form reads the change back in a sheet before saving (title, Was and Will be, a change of source alone showing the two sources, the goals named, the six first then “and {k} more”); `save_metric` takes `comparable`, `reason` and `relabel`, and with fewer decimals names the goals that show more (`moreDecimals`).

**Rule 9. Marks** (`marksFor(metric, link, since, until)`). A save with the number changed (`comparable: false`) or a new direction keeps a mark on the metric: `{ week, at, by, kind: definition | direction, why, was, now }`, oldest first. A goal shows the marks made at or after it was linked, in its own cycle (since it began and before the day after its last week, so a change made next year leaves this year's goals alone; only this cycle's goals are told in History): on its chart a dashed hairline at the week labelled beside it (“Definition changed, week {w}”, “Direction changed, week {w}”, through the core's `goal.marks` point), in its History the entry with the reason, and under About the line with “See both definitions”. Undo takes the mark back with the change.

**Rule 10. Retire, bring back, merge** (`retireMetric`, `unretireMetric`, `mergeMetrics`, `everUsed`). A metric that has ever measured a goal (`everUsed`) can't be deleted: “{name} has measured goals, so it can’t be deleted. Retire it instead.” Its owner or an admin retires it with a reason (and optionally a live metric in the same unit that replaces it): its links stay, its goals keep their numbers and say “Measured by {metric}, retired {date}”, it leaves `liveMetrics` (the pickers and the library's list) but `measureOf` and `findMetric` still find it, and no new goal can be linked to it. The library lists retired ones apart (`?retired=1`, “See the {n} retired metrics” under the list), and a new metric with a retired one's name is refused in words that say it is retired, with a link to it. Bring it back clears the four fields. Admins merge a live metric into another live one in the same unit: every live link moves (same slice and part), the first is retired pointing to the second, and each moved goal's History says so. Each is one save with one Undo.

### Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Lead time for changes (1 goal): its caveats reworded. | `words` |
| Lead time for changes: its meaning changed. | `meaning` |
| Lead time for changes: hours to min, not said to be a label. | `scale` |
| Rhea changes what Lead time for changes means and says the number itself changes, with no reason. | `refused: Say why, in a line. Every goal measured by it will show this.` |
| Rhea deletes Lead time for changes, which measures a goal. | `refused: Lead time for changes has measured goals, so it can’t be deleted. Retire it instead.` |
| Rhea retires Flaky test rate: “The test platform reports it now.” | `Retired the metric “Flaky test rate”: The test platform reports it now. / Its metric “Flaky test rate” was retired: The test platform reports it now.` |
| Rhea, not an admin, merges Flaky test rate into Remote build cache hit rate. | `refused: Only admins can merge metrics: it changes what other people’s goals are measured by.` |

### Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** The mark’s week is the cycle week the change is saved in; a change saved between cycles marks week 0 of the next.
- **Not self-explanatory:** Merging two metrics in different directions is a Check on the form (“Merge anyway”), not a rule: the rule merges either way.
- **Not self-explanatory:** Marks on a chart: two in one week are one line with both labels, and only the latest three weeks are drawn (the core’s `goalMarksOf`); History keeps them all.

### Where it lives

- [src/modules/metrics/rulesChange.ts](../../../src/modules/metrics/rulesChange.ts): `changeKinds`, `linkedGoals`, `aimingWrong`, `saveMetricChange`, `retireMetric`, `unretireMetric`, `mergeMetrics`, `retiredWords`
- [src/modules/metrics/rules.ts](../../../src/modules/metrics/rules.ts): `everUsed`, `marksFor`, `markLabel`, `liveMetrics`, `removeMetric`

### Requirements

- `METRIC-CHANGE`: A metric that changes tells its goals (MT3). Changing a metric goals use reads back what it does to them first: a new meaning or source asks "Is it still the same number?"; "The number itself changes" and a new direction each need a reason, and leave a mark on every goal's chart ("Definition changed, week {w}", a dashed hairline labelled beside it) and History; a new unit is a new label (every goal's unit changes too) or a different scale, refused. A metric that has measured a goal is retired, not deleted: its goals keep their links and numbers and say "Measured by {metric}, retired {date}", it leaves the pickers, and Bring it back undoes it. Admins merge a metric into another in the same unit, moving its goals and retiring it pointing there. Every one of these saves with one Undo, and retire_metric, merge_metrics and save_metric's comparable, reason and relabel do the same through MCP.

## Measured, partly measured or a gap

Whether a metric is measured today (rule 11), what the library does with a gap or a part, and the goals a gap holds to no number: the library fills in the goal’s field; the core’s rule reads it.

### The rule

**Rule 11. Measured, Partly or Gap** (`measurementOf`, `measurementProblems`). Each metric says whether its number is measured today: `measured` (in full, every time it is due; the default, and what a metric never said otherwise is), `partly` (some of it, or not every period) or `gap` (nobody measures it yet), with an optional line on what is missing and who is sorting it out (at most 300 characters; kept only while not measured). It is always shown as a shape and its word: a filled square (Measured), a half-filled square (Partly), a broken square (Gap). Its owner or an admin says it, as any other field; History logs it as “Measured”.

**To sort out** (`metricNeeds`). A gap comes first in what a metric needs: “Not measured yet: {n} goals held to no number” (the goals it measures now; “Not measured yet” with none); a part: “Only partly measured”. Each with “Say how it’s measured”, which opens the form at that field. The library’s “Something to sort out” filter lists them with the rest.

**Held to no number** (`heldBy`, `heldByLink`; the core's `isUnmeasured`). A goal measured by a metric with a gap is held to no number: the goal's own field `unmeasuredSince` is set, and the core's status rule reads it (never the library). The library sets and clears it, in the same save as the cause, with a line in the goal's History and one Undo:
- a metric saved as a gap holds every goal it measures now (a live link; the goal neither removed nor stopped; not one with dated stages): “Held to no number until “{metric}” is measured”;
- the metric saved as measured or partly lets go of them: “Held to its plan again, as “{metric}” is measured”;
- a goal linked to a gap is held; linked to a measured metric, or unlinked, it is let go (“Held to its plan again”).
A save that leaves the gap as it was writes no goal.

### Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Flaky test rate, never said otherwise. | `Measured` |
| Rhea says Flaky test rate is a gap: “The new runners send no results yet.” | `Changed the metric “Flaky test rate” / Held to no number until “Flaky test rate” is measured` |
| Rhea says what is missing from Flaky test rate in 301 characters. | `refused: Keep what’s missing to 300 characters or fewer.` |
| Flaky test rate as a gap, measuring one goal: what it needs first. | `gap: Not measured yet: 1 goal held to no number → Say how it’s measured` |

### Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** A partly measured metric holds its goals to their plans: the part that is measured is the number. Say what is missing so readers know.
- **Not self-explanatory:** The goal side asks for no baseline only once a goal may be saved without one (backlog GB and BL); until then a goal held to no number keeps the plan it was given, unjudged.

### Where it lives

- [src/modules/metrics/rulesMeasured.ts](../../../src/modules/metrics/rulesMeasured.ts): `measurementOf`, `holdsToNoNumber`, `measurementProblems`, `measurementWords`, `heldBy`, `heldByLink`
- [src/modules/metrics/rulesLibrary.ts](../../../src/modules/metrics/rulesLibrary.ts): `metricNeeds`
- [src/domain/unmeasured.ts](../../../src/domain/unmeasured.ts): `isUnmeasured`, `heldToNoNumber`

### Requirements

- `METRIC-MEASUREMENT`: A gap in measurement is visible and owned, not faked (MS). Each metric says whether it is measured today, Measured, Partly or Gap, always as a shape (a filled, half-filled or broken square) and its word, with an optional line on what is missing (at most 300 characters). A metric with a gap or measured only in part is listed under To sort out on its page and in the library ("Not measured yet: {n} goals held to no number", "Only partly measured") with Say how it's measured. A goal measured by a metric with a gap is held to no number: it says Not measured yet (a broken ring and the words) instead of a status, nothing on it is due, late or quiet, and it projects nothing; linking it to a measured metric, unlinking it, or its metric being measured holds it to its plan again, in the same save, with one Undo and a line in its History. save_metric takes measurement and measurement_note, and get_metric and the export say so.

## A reading in a check-in

Where a metric’s number comes from can fill in a goal’s check-in (NR): which state the number step is in, and what a check-in records of what the source said. A person confirms every number; nothing is ever posted for them.

### The rule

A **number source** (`NumberSource`, the module's port) reads a metric, optionally for a link's **slice** (`{ teamId, part }`: a team or the whole company, and a part or all of it). A source that reads only the whole company reads no team's slice: a company-wide number is never put in a team's goal. `read(metric, at, slice)` gives the latest reading measured at or before `at` (`{ value, at }`, `at` when the source measured it), null when it has none, and throws only when it can't be reached. The step asks once when it opens (`askSource`); a source whose `reads` throws, that takes more than 5 seconds, or whose answer isn't a finite number measured at a time that parses and isn't after now, is unreachable.

**Rule 1. A reading's state** (`readingState(reading, lastReading, lastValue, now, typed, decimals)`). The first that applies: **no-slice**, the source reads the metric but not this slice; **unreachable**, it threw; **missing**, no reading; **old**, measured more than 7 days before now (one limit for every metric, and an old value is never offered); **same**, the goal's latest check-in recorded a reading measured at or after this one; **jump**, the reading is ten times or a tenth of the last number (by size; from a last number of 0, a size of 10 or more); **changed**, the owner typed a number that differs from the reading at the metric's decimals; otherwise **fresh**. `readingRevised` says when the source, asked again for the last reading's moment, now gives another number.

**Rule 2. What is recorded** (`recordReading`, the core's `CheckIn.reading`). `{ source, value, at, why? }`: the source's name, what it said and when it measured it; `why` (`behind`, `other-count`, `wrong` or `else` with words) only when the check-in's number differs. The check-in's `value` is always the owner's number. Nothing that judges a goal (its status, flags, attention or order) reads it. Saved only when set (migration 0047's nullable `reading`).

**The number step** (the core's place `checkin.number`, drawn by `CheckInNumber` in the module's own chunk; nothing in the first download). Drawn when the goal is measured by a metric a registered source reads; the source is asked once when the step opens, never on Home. Each state of rule 1 is one row: **fresh**, the field holds the reading at the goal's places (a number filled in isn't the owner's: a draft reopened on this step with it untouched is filled again from what the source says then), "From {source}, read {when}." and "Week {w}: {last}. Change the number if it’s wrong, and you’ll be asked why. You still say what changed: that is the next step.", the primary "Confirm {value} {unit}", and "No new number this week"; **changed**, the owner's number, "You typed {typed}. {source} said {value}, read {when}." with "Put {value} back", "Why is it different?" (the four reasons of `READING_WHY`; "Say more" is needed only with "Something else", at least 10 characters) and "Kept with this check-in, beside what {source} said. It doesn’t change the goal’s status and nobody is told.", the primary "Use {typed} {unit}", waiting until a reason is chosen; **same**, empty, "No new reading since your last check-in: {source} still says {value}, read {when}.", the primary "No new number this week" and "Type a different number"; **old**, empty, the warning mark and "{source} last read this on {date}, {n} days ago. That is too old to fill in. Type this week’s number, or say there isn’t one.", with no old value anywhere; **no-slice**, empty, "{source} measures this for the whole company, not for {team} on its own, so it isn’t filled in." and the goal's "Where to get it"; **missing**, "{source} has no number for this yet. Type this week’s number."; **unreachable**, "{source} couldn’t be reached just now. Type the number, or try again." with Try again; **jump**, a Check: "{source} says {value}. That is ten times (a tenth of) week {w}’s {last}. Is it right?", "Yes, confirm {value}" or "Type a different number". "Read {when}" is in the viewer's zone (`readWhen`): "9:02 today", "16:40 yesterday", otherwise "9:00 on Thu 5 Nov". With a source involved the step drops "Typed in by hand."; with the module off the step is as it always was. A confirmed reading answers the step's own "the same as last week?".

**Rule 3. The same rule everywhere** (`readingProblem`, `keptReading`: the core engine's, in `planChanges`). A reading goes with a check-in from the form (`CheckInPost.reading`), the one table (each row's) and the AI tool (`readings` beside its row); the engine refuses one whose number differs from the check-in's with no reason ("{source} said {value}. Say why your number is different."), or "Something else" with under 10 characters; it also refuses a reason's words over 500 characters, a reading whose number isn't finite, and one measured at a time that doesn't parse, after now or more than 7 days before it; and it keeps the reason only when the numbers differ. A week's check-in saved again with no reading keeps the one it had only while its number is unchanged; every check-in row writes `reading`, null when there is none, so a database never keeps a stale one. post_check_in takes `reading_confirmed` (the owner confirmed the number the source reads now; `value` may then be left out, and is the reading at the goal's places) and `different_because` (`{ kind, text }`): the server asks the same source (`readForTool`) and records what rule 1 calls fresh or changed, comparing at the goal's places as the engine does; both are for this week's check-in only (a source reads what it says now), so with an earlier `week` they are refused; without them nothing is read or recorded, as with the import. With the module off it says the module-off sentence.

**The read-back** (`readingLine`): the check-in's receipt gains "{value} {unit}, from {source}, read {when}. Confirmed by you." or "{typed} {unit}, typed. {source} said {value} {unit}: {reason in lower case}."

**Where it shows elsewhere** (NR3; the words are the core's, `src/domain/reading.ts`, since the record is the core's `CheckIn.reading`; Faro keeps no series of readings, so each place says what a check-in recorded). The goal's **Measured by** gains "This week’s number" from its latest check-in (`readingThisWeek`): "{value} {unit}, from {source}, read {when}. Confirmed by {name}." or "{typed} {unit}, typed by {name}. {source} said {value} {unit}.", and nothing when it recorded none. Each **History** row's second line (`readingHistoryLine`): "From {source}, read {when}. {name} checked in." or "Typed by {name}. {source} said {value} {unit}. {Reason}: “{words}”", and "Typed by {name}." on a goal any of whose check-ins was filled in. A **review's agenda** row says " · from {source}" after a confirmed number, in the quiet ink, and nothing after a typed one (`readingFrom`: no mark, no flag). The **Check-ins sheet** gains Number from ("Typed", or the source), Source’s number, Measured at (ISO, UTC) and Reason for a different number after Value, worked out or for reading and never loaded back (`readingCells`). get_goal's check-ins carry `numberFrom` with History's line.

**Rule 4. The metric's page** (`fillsIn`, `differentNumbers`). Under "Where the number comes from", for a metric that names a source, "In each goal’s check-in" lists its goals (Goal, For, In its check-in): **filled**, a registered source reads the metric for the goal's slice, "Filled in from {source} · last read {when}" (when the goal's latest recorded reading was measured; left out before any); **no-slice**, one reads it but not that slice, "Typed by hand: {source} has no number per team"; **none**, "Typed by hand: no source can be read". No source is asked. Under it, per source, the check-ins of the metric's goals in the last 8 weeks up to this week (removed ones aside) that recorded a reading from it are `n`, and those whose number isn't the reading's at the goal's decimals are `k`: "In the last 8 weeks, {k} of {n} check-ins filled in from {source} used a different number." with "See them", the goals and weeks (each opening that goal's History at the week). It names goals and weeks, never people; get_metric gives the same (`inItsCheckIn` on each goal, `differentNumbers`).

**The one table** (the core's place `checkin.table`, `CheckInTableReadings`): a goal not yet checked in this week whose reading is fresh shows it in its cell in the quiet ink, with "From {source}, read {when}." and "Confirm {value}" under it. **A filled-in number needs a touch (Lane, 13 Nov):** an untouched row isn't posted; the owner confirms it with one tap ("Confirm {value}"), or all of them with "Confirm all readings" (two or more), or types over it. Under the table, "{n} numbers are filled in from their sources. Confirm each, or change it: one nobody confirms isn't posted." (one: "1 number is filled in from its source. Confirm it, or change it: it isn't posted until you do."). The same rule at every door: post_check_in posts a source's number only with `reading_confirmed`, and the import reads no source, so it never posts one. A cell changed from its reading asks "Why is it different from what {source} said ({value})?" in its row before it counts as ready. Nothing is posted that the owner did not post.

**The demo's sources** (`demoSources`, made by `sourcesFrom` from the example as the demo built it, before this browser's saves; a workspace of your own has none). "CI analytics" reads CI pipeline time on main (p90) for the whole company; "CI runner metrics" reads Pipeline queue wait (p90) for CI/CD · main branch pipelines and Build & Release · release pipelines. Each is a seeded series made once from the example as it was seeded, never from later check-ins: the numbers of the goal it follows by week, continued one week, measured at 09:00 UTC on the review day; release pipelines has no reading in the last week, and an eval fixture can make every series two weeks behind (`?sources=behind` in the check-in's address). On the server, the AI tool's sources are made from the example's check-ins before this week.

### Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Now Thu 12 Nov 10:00: 12 min at Thu 09:02; the last check-in 13, typed. | `fresh` |
| The same, and the owner types 14. | `changed` |
| The same, and the owner types 12.0. | `fresh` |
| 13 min at Mon 2 Nov. | `old` |
| 13 min at Fri 6 Nov 09:00, which week 45’s check-in recorded. | `same` |
| 13 min at Thu 5 Nov 09:00, which week 45’s check-in recorded (7 days and an hour). | `old` |
| The link is for CI/CD; the source reads the whole company only. | `no-slice` |
| 130 at Thu 09:02; the last number 13. | `jump` |
| Rule 3: CI analytics said 12; the owner posts 14 with no reason. | `CI analytics said 12. Say why your number is different.` |
| Rule 3: the same, “Something else: moved”. | `Say more about why your number is different from what CI analytics said, in at least 10 characters.` |
| The read-back: 14 min typed, CI analytics said 12 min, the source counts something else. | `14 min, typed. CI analytics said 12 min: the source counts something else.` |
| Rule 4: a goal measured for CI/CD by a metric CI analytics reads only for the whole company. | `Typed by hand: CI analytics has no number per team` |
| Rule 4: in the last 8 weeks, 12 and 15 typed over 12 and 13 from CI analytics. | `In the last 8 weeks, 1 of 2 check-ins filled in from CI analytics used a different number.` |
| History: 15 min typed by Rhea Kapoor; CI analytics said 13 min; it counts something else. | `Typed by Rhea Kapoor. CI analytics said 13 min. The source counts something else.` |
| Recorded: CI analytics said 12 at Thu 09:02; the owner used 14 because the source is behind. | `{"source":"CI analytics","value":12,"at":"2026-11-12T09:02:00Z","why":{"kind":"behind"}}` |

### Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** NR’s table gives 120 against a last 13 as a jump; MT4’s Check, which NR keeps, is ten times or more, and 120 is 9.2 times, so it is fresh: the example here uses 130.
- **Not self-explanatory:** On the server the demo’s sources are made from the example’s check-ins before this week, not the example as first built (the server can’t rebuild it); a correction of an earlier week there moves the series.
- **Not self-explanatory:** The 8-week count shows whenever a check-in was filled in from the source, “0 of n” included, and See them only when some used a different number. See them opens a list of goals and weeks, each linking to that goal’s History at the week, rather than one History across goals (none exists).
- **Not self-explanatory:** The demo has one goal on each read slice; Build & Release · release pipelines is read but no goal is linked to it yet.

### Requirements

- `READING-PREFILL`: When a goal is measured by a metric that a registered number source reads for the link's own slice (its team and part), the check-in's number step asks the source once when it opens and fills the field with the latest reading: "From {source}, read {when}." (in the viewer's zone: "9:02 today", "16:40 yesterday", else "9:00 on Thu 5 Nov") and the step's primary names the number ("Confirm 12 min"). Nothing is ever posted for the owner: a week with a reading and no check-in has no check-in. A source that reads only the whole company never fills in a team's goal ("{source} measures this for the whole company, not for {team} on its own, so it isn't filled in."); no source, no number yet, nothing new since the last check-in and a source that can't be reached each say so, and the step is otherwise as without a source. With the Metric library off, the step is exactly as it was.
- `READING-RECORDED-ONLY`: A number typed over a reading asks "Why is it different?" with four choices (the source is behind: I have a newer number; counts something else; is wrong this week; something else, which needs at least 10 characters of Say more) before "Use {typed} {unit}". The owner's number is the check-in's; the reading (source, value, when measured) and the reason are recorded beside it, by the same rule at every door (the form, the one table, post_check_in's reading_confirmed and different_because), and the read-back says "{value}, from {source}, read {when}. Confirmed by you." or "{typed}, typed. {source} said {value}: {reason}." Nothing reads the reason to decide a status, a flag, an attention count or an order: no review flag, no mark against the owner.
- `READING-SEVEN-DAYS`: A reading more than 7 days old (RULES.readingMaxDays, one limit for every metric) is not filled in and its value is not shown anywhere on the step: "{source} last read this on {date}, {n} days ago. That is too old to fill in. Type this week's number, or say there isn't one." with the warning mark, the step's Continue and No new number this week.
- `READING-SHOWN`: Where a check-in's number came from shows beyond the check-in, from what the check-in recorded (Faro keeps no series of readings): the goal's Measured by says "This week's number" from its latest check-in ("{value}, from {source}, read {when}. Confirmed by {name}." or "{typed}, typed by {name}. {source} said {value}.", nothing when it recorded none); each History row says "From {source}, read {when}. {name} checked in." or "Typed by {name}. {source} said {value}. {Reason}: “{words}”"; the metric's page lists its goals with "In its check-in" ("Filled in from {source} · last read {when}", "Typed by hand: {source} has no number per team" or "Typed by hand: no source can be read") and "In the last 8 weeks, {k} of {n} check-ins filled in from {source} used a different number." with See them (goals and weeks, never people); a review's agenda row says "· from {source}" in the quiet ink after a confirmed number, and nothing for a typed one; the Check-ins sheet has Number from, Source's number, Measured at and Reason for a different number, for reading, never loaded back; get_goal and get_metric say the same.
